article.title: Elena Rybakina Wins US Open 2026 and Becomes World No. 1
article.description: Elena Rybakina defeated Aryna Sabalenka to win her first US Open title, claim her third Grand Slam and officially take over the world No. 1 ranking.
article.dek: Rybakina came to New York with an injury concern. She left with the US Open trophy, a record prize and the No. 1 ranking.
article.intro: Elena Rybakina arrived at the US Open with questions surrounding her fitness. She left New York with something far bigger than answers. The 27-year-old from Kazakhstan defeated two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 to capture her first US Open championship. The victory also completed a remarkable rise to the top of women's tennis. But the scoreline only tells part of the story. Behind Rybakina's breakthrough was a comeback from an injury scare, a dramatic semifinal against American favorite Coco Gauff, and a final against the woman who had dominated New York for the previous two years.

sections.heading: From Injury Doubt to the Biggest Stage
paragraphs: Just days before the US Open began, Rybakina's participation was not completely certain. She had retired from her Cincinnati quarterfinal against Iga Swiatek after experiencing ankle problems, raising questions about whether she would be physically ready for another Grand Slam campaign.

Instead of backing away from the challenge, Rybakina steadily built momentum in New York. She reached the quarterfinals without dropping a set and then fought back from a set down to defeat Qinwen Zheng. That victory had another major consequence: Rybakina secured the No. 1 ranking for the first time in her career.
She came to New York wondering how far her body would let her go. Soon, the question became whether anyone could stop her.

sections.heading: Then Came Coco Gauff
paragraphs: The path to the final became even more difficult when Rybakina faced American star Coco Gauff in the semifinal. Gauff won the opening set 6-3 in front of a packed Arthur Ashe Stadium. For an American crowd hoping to see another homegrown champion reach the final, the momentum appeared to be going in one direction.

Rybakina had other plans. She adjusted her game, reduced her errors and fought back to win the second set 6-4. In the deciding set, she kept her composure and closed out the match to reach her first US Open final.
For Rybakina, it was another example of what had become the defining quality of her tournament: staying calm when the pressure was highest.
The New York crowd had a favorite. Rybakina had a different idea.

sections.heading: Sabalenka Wanted History. Rybakina Took It Away.
paragraphs: The final was a showdown between the world's two biggest stories. Sabalenka arrived in New York as the two-time defending champion and was trying to become the first woman since Serena Williams to win three consecutive US Open titles. Rybakina, meanwhile, was already guaranteed to become the new world No. 1.
The match lived up to the hype. Rybakina won the opening set 6-4, but Sabalenka answered by taking the second 7-5. Everything came down to the final set.

That was when Rybakina produced her most important tennis of the tournament. She broke through Sabalenka's defenses, remained composed and won the deciding set 6-2. The victory ended Sabalenka's 19-match US Open winning streak and stopped her attempt at a historic three-peat.
One set separated Rybakina from history. She played it like she had nothing to lose.

sections.heading: A New No. 1 Has Arrived
paragraphs: When the final point was over, Rybakina had accomplished something extraordinary. She had won her first US Open title, her third Grand Slam championship, and her second major of 2026 after winning the Australian Open earlier this year.

She also became the first player from Kazakhstan — man or woman — to reach the top of the world rankings. WTA confirmed that she would officially become No. 1 when the rankings were updated after the tournament.
And then came another remarkable number: $5.5 million. That was Rybakina's prize for winning the tournament, the largest prize in Grand Slam history.

For someone who entered the tournament with questions about her ankle, the ending could hardly have been more dramatic. New York didn't just give Rybakina another trophy. It gave women's tennis a new No. 1.

article.closing: Elena Rybakina's 2026 US Open run was more than another Grand Slam victory. It was a story of responding to doubt, surviving pressure and finishing when the biggest moment arrived. She entered New York chasing a title. She left as US Open champion and the new No. 1 player in women's tennis. And after everything that happened in those two weeks, one thing is clear: Elena Rybakina has arrived at the top — and she may not be finished climbing.
